duplicate_notes: CONFIRMED DUPLICATE (resolved 2026-07-10 via live GSM-level verification, upgraded from 'possible/unresolved'): direct comparison of individual GSM sample titles proves GSE168726 and GSE180061 contain the IDENTICAL 121-sample cohort, not two distinct sample sets. Every specimen ID matches 1:1 across both accessions -- e.g. GSM5159926 in this series is titled 'CAM20.0001' (tissue: fresh-frozen human meningioma, molecule subtype: bisulfite-treated DNA), and the corresponding GSM5452060 in GSE180061 is titled 'Tumor methylation_CAM20.0001' with identical tissue/molecule-subtype characteristics; the same match holds at the other end of both sample lists (GSM5160046='CAM20.0156' here vs. GSM5452180='Tumor methylation_CAM20.0156' in GSE180061). This is the same underlying 121-sample Princess Margaret Cancer Center meningioma methylation cohort deposited twice under two different GEO accessions: this one (GSE168726, submitted 2021-03-11, public 2022-03-30, no linked PMID) and GSE180061 (submitted 2021-07-13, public 2021-07-14, linked to Nassiri et al. Nature 2021, PMID 34433969). GSE180061 is the accession actually linked to the published paper and should be treated as the canonical/citable accession; this record (GSE168726) is a redundant duplicate deposit of the same 121 specimens. Not auto-merged into a single corpus record in this pass (both accessions are kept as separate entries per the corpus's dedup policy), but downstream analyses should avoid double-counting these 121 patients across both records.
